intro: How Land and Buildings Transaction Tax works for residential purchases in Scotland: the bands, first-time buyer relief and the Additional Dwelling Supplement on extra homes.
explanation:
## Each LBTT rate applies only to the slice of the price inside its band

Scottish buyers pay Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (LBTT) rather than Stamp Duty Land Tax. A purchase at or below {fact:lbtt_nil_rate_threshold} owes nothing. Above that, the rate climbs from {fact:lbtt_band_2pct} up to {fact:lbtt_band_12pct}, and each rate is charged only on the part of the price that falls inside its band.

A return has to be sent to Revenue Scotland for most residential purchases of £40,000 or more, even when no tax turns out to be due.

## First-time buyers have a higher nil-rate band

First-time buyer relief lifts the nil-rate band to {fact:lbtt_ftb_nil_rate_threshold}. For a buyer who qualifies, that cuts the bill by up to £600.

## The Additional Dwelling Supplement is charged on the whole price

Buying an additional home, such as a second home, a rental property or a holiday home, can bring a supplement of {fact:lbtt_ads_rate}. Unlike the bands, it is worked out on the entire purchase price and added on top of any LBTT. The trigger is already owning at least one home, wherever in the world it is, while buying another that does not replace the buyer's only or main residence. A home used by family or friends counts, even when no rent is charged. Where there are several buyers, one of them owning a home is enough.

Companies and other buyers that are not individuals normally pay it on residential purchases even when they own nothing else.

The supplement does not apply when:

- the buyer owns only one home at the end of the purchase day, or the price is under £40,000
- the buyer has sold their only or main home in the 36 months before buying a replacement main home
- the only other property owned, or the owner's share of a jointly owned one, is worth less than £40,000

A repayment of the supplement can be claimed if the previous main home is sold within 36 months of buying the replacement and the buyer has lived in the replacement as their only or main residence. The rules differ slightly for joint buyers.

## England and Northern Ireland use Stamp Duty Land Tax instead

Stamp Duty Land Tax applies in England and Northern Ireland, with different bands. For comparison, its standard nil-rate threshold is {fact:sdlt_nil_rate_threshold}.
meta_description: Scottish residential LBTT is nil up to {fact:lbtt_nil_rate_threshold}, with higher bands above it, first-time buyer relief and an additional dwelling supplement of {fact:lbtt_ads_rate}.
